title: SDK resilience, tool-emulation, and offline contract notes
body:
Context / motivation:

We ship a streaming-first Hosted API. In practice customers operate in environments with intermittent networks (mobile, slow corporate proxies) and with complex tool graphs (search, database, external actions). We need an SDK surface and runtime patterns that: keep developer ergonomics simple, avoid surprising client-level failures, and let products degrade gracefully (rather than error loudly) while preserving deterministic reconciliation when connectivity returns.

This doc collects notes and concrete proposals for three related topics that often show up together in product feedback: SDK resilience behaviors, tool-emulation (local stub) modes for offline/fast-path UX, and a compact offline contract/journal format for session reconciliation. This is intentionally a working draft — experimental ideas + tradeoffs.

Key goals:
- Keep developer API minimal: easy opt-in hooks rather than extensive callbacks.
- Predictable reconciliation: developers can deterministically re-run or reconcile partial outputs with server authority.
- Minimal server changes: prefer client-side fallbacks that work with existing stream framing where possible.
- Observable and debuggable: telemetry for when fallbacks/emulation/reconciles happen.

Design primitives (vocab):
- frame: an incremental unit emitted by the hosted stream (text delta, tool-call start/end, metadata).
- soft-resume: resume where left off without re-executing side effects, using journaled frames + server-authoritative merge.
- toollet: a small tool invocation (search, fetch, exec) treated as a transaction with idempotent semantics.
- emulation-mode: SDK-local stub behavior for toollets that supplies cached or synthesized results instead of invoking remote endpoints.
- journal: compact append-only record of frames and toollet outcomes used for offline replay/reconciliation.

Proposed SDK ergonomics (API sketch, high-level):
- default client mode = streaming-first with optimistic partial output and auto-retry.
- lightweight config knobs exposed via init: { maxBufferedFrames, fallbackPolicy, emulateToolOnNetworkLoss, journalRetentionMs }
- API helpers: 
  - session.start({journalId?, resumeFrom?}) -> sessionHandle
  - session.on('frame', cb) // streaming incremental frames
  - session.commit() // marks final commit for server-side audit
  - session.reconcile() -> Promise<{replayDiffs}> // ask server to reconcile local journal with authoritative stream
  - session.setToolEmulator(toolName, emulatorFn) // dev provides local stub

Example usage patterns:
- Mobile app: enable emulateToolOnNetworkLoss=true and provide small local emulators for search/autosuggest so the assistant can complete short tasks while offline.
- Enterprise client behind heavy proxy: increase maxBufferedFrames and switch fallbackPolicy to 'sync-fallback' so server returns a synchronous final result if streaming stalls.

Tool-emulation specifics:
- Emulators must be pure functions that return a deterministic result given (toolName, args, toolId). SDK will record the emulator output in the journal with a special flag (emulated=true).
- When connectivity returns, the SDK will call session.reconcile(). Server will accept the emulated result if either: (a) tool is side-effect-free (search, read-only DB), or (b) developer marked the toollet as idempotent/confirmable. Otherwise server responds with authoritative result and server-suggested repair actions.
- Guarantee model: never perform side-effecting tool calls locally unless developer explicitly marks tool as safe_local_side_effect. Even then, surface a clear warning and require explicit opt-in.

Offline journal / contract (compact)
- Journal is append-only sequence of records: [frame_meta, frame_payload_base64, toollet_outcome_hash, signature?] — keep small, base64 payload for binary attachments only.
- Minimal fields per record: timestamp, frame_id, session_id, type (partial_text|tool_call|commit_marker), payload (string), tool_meta (tool_id, idempotent_flag), emulated (true/false), reconcile_status (pending/resolved).
- On reconcile, client posts journal diffs to /sessions/{id}/reconcile. Server returns {accepted_frames:[], conflicts:[{frame_id, server_payload, suggested_action}], final_session_state}.

Streaming->sync fallback modes (behaviors):
- degrade: keep streaming on the wire but buffer > Xms and then switch client to request a synchronous final payload for remaining prompt. Server runtime builds a fast finalization snapshot. This avoids client-side infinite waits.
- local-stub: if network loss is detected (>= N failed heartbeats) and emulateToolOnNetworkLoss enabled, use emulators for toollets and issue soft-resume later.
- hedged-sync: issue short hedged synchronous requests to another region/cheap model when streaming stalls beyond latency SLO. Good for high-importance flows.

Telemetry surface (what we should capture):
- session.journal.size_bytes (how big local journals are)
- session.emulation.used (boolean / counter) and session.emulation.sources (which emulator was used)
- session.reconcile.latency and reconcile.conflicts.count
- frame.drop.reason and frame.drop.count
- fallback.invoked with fallbackPolicy and trigger (network|backpressure|manual)

Developer UX considerations and constraints:
- Keep default behavior safe: all local emulation should be disabled by default for safety-sensitive tools.
- Make emulation path auditable: any emulation must add clear metadata to frames so server and product logs differentiate synthesized vs authoritative results.
- Console integration: in Console, surface a timeline that shows emulated frames vs server frames so customers can debug session anomalies.
- Storage: journals should be compact by default; SDK offers pruning policy. Explicit opt-in to persist journals beyond session lifetime.

Edge cases and tradeoffs (non-exhaustive):
- conflict rate: optimistic emulation for read-only tools will often be accepted, but ambiguous cases where emulation diverges (e.g., search results changed) create UX churn during reconciliation. We must measure conflict frequency across customers.
- GDPR/PII: local journals may leak sensitive prompts; default SDK should encrypt journals with platform-provided KMS or not persist unless explicitly enabled.
- cost: hedged-sync increases server compute; expose budget/hedge limits in SDK config.
- server changes: to fully support commit/reconcile flow we need a small server endpoint to accept compact journals and compute diffs. Minimal server-side work but required for deterministic soft-resume.

Open questions (to resolve in follow-ups):
- What is the canonical reconciliation API? payload shape, rate limits, and backpressure semantics. (PROD-1284 linked)
- How to express partial trust for tools? We currently have idempotent_flag; is a richer trust model needed (confidence, TTL)?
- Storage/retention: default retention for journals — 24h, 7d, config? Tradeoffs between debugability and storage cost.
- UX at scale: how will Console expose thousands of reconcile conflicts? Need compact clusterable views.

Immediate next steps / actionable checklist:
- [ ] Spike: implement a reference SDK emulator shim in JS + small demo mobile app that uses search & calendar emulators. (owner: Diego) — 2w
- [ ] Backend: design reconcile endpoint + diff algorithm, draft API spec for PROD-1284 (owner: Lena) — 1w
- [ ] Telemetry: add emulation and reconcile metrics to instrumentation plan (owner: Ian) — 3d
- [ ] Security: write brief for local journal encryption/consent in Private deployments (owner: Security) — 1w
- [ ] UX: mock Console timeline showing emulated frames vs server frames (owner: Design) — 1w

Notes to self / rough ideas: 
- Could experiment with a small canonical 'emulation vocabulary' to let emulators return lightweight structured summaries instead of full blobs (saves journal bandwidth).
- Consider CLI adaptor: a thin tool that can be run locally in dev-mode to replay journals and produce server-expected reconcile payloads for offline debugging.
- If we lock down the journal format early, we can reuse it for cost-aware caching in Redwood Optimize later (analytics on conflict patterns).

References & links:
- Jira: PROD-1284 (reconciliation API design)
- Reference PR: github.com/redwood-inference/redwood-sdk/pull/742 (starter for emulator hooks)
- Slack: #dev-hosted-api thread: emulation-edgecases (link above)

End of draft. Feedback requested: prioritize server reconcile API vs richer client-only heuristics? My leaning: deliver a minimal reconcile endpoint (accept compact journals, return diffs) + client-side emulation prototype for read-only tools.
